Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

Pre-ruling historical artifact. H2 is still an active hypothesis in this snapshot; no final ruling is recorded here.

ACTIVE HYPOTHESIS
The spike may reflect a competitor cycle targeting the mid-segment base, ordinary February seasonality, or a related calendar effect. The test is whether the current mid-segment monthly-churn reading has a comparable historical same-window pattern or a dated external event that makes the increase unsurprising. Marcus’s pricing-page experiment is a separate parallel track and must not be used as evidence for or against H2.

PLANNED HISTORICAL COMPARISON WORK
- Re-run current and historical cuts with the same cohort logic used in the January scan, with Owen’s validation.
- Line up same-window monthly churn by segment, keeping mid-segment explicitly identified.
- Place historical comparisons directly beside the current read so the “weird February month” explanation is testable rather than assumed.
- Overlay only market or competitor events with an actual timestamp; do not fill gaps with undated competitor narrative.
- Complete one final denominator-handling sanity check before converting the directional read into a ruling.
- Keep the metric of record fixed as monthly churn and preserve the v1 50–200-seat definition for this historical artifact.

AGREED HYPOTHESIS-RULING ONE-PAGER CONTRACT
Owner for every hypothesis-ruling one-pager: Owen. Each one-pager must state the hypothesis and rationale, cohort and denominator definition, analytical cuts, p-values and/or effect sizes where applicable, the ruling/call, and the material caveats or data-quality checks. The one-pagers are decision records, not loose exploratory notes.

H1 — PRICING ARTIFACT
Owner: Owen.
Contents: rationale for the packaging, discounting, or contract-mix explanation; mid-segment churn split by entry, standard, and plus tiers; relevant pricing/contract-mix cuts; p-values and/or effect sizes where applicable; explicit ruling/call. Marcus’s pricing-page experiment remains separate and is not substituted for this analysis.

H2 — COMPETITOR CYCLE / SEASONALITY
Owner: Owen.
Contents: rationale for the competitor-cycle and February-seasonality explanations; same-window monthly-churn comparisons by segment using the January-scan cohort logic; dated market and competitor-event overlay; denominator-handling validation; p-values and/or effect sizes where applicable; explicit ruling/call. This pre-ruling brief records the planned work, not the later result.

H3 — ONBOARDING TIMING
Owner: Owen.
Contents: rationale that late-December/early-January starts may mature into lagged churn; activation timing cuts at day 0, day 3, and day 7; comparison of accounts activated before the day-7 touch with accounts still unactivated at day 7; p-values and/or effect sizes where applicable; explicit ruling/call; limitations on causal interpretation.

H4 — CS COVERAGE GAP
Owner: Owen.
Contents: rationale that CSM load or coverage drift may have left accounts underserved; coverage and assignment math; workload/coverage changes over the relevant period; churn cuts by coverage exposure or gap where supportable; p-values and/or effect sizes where applicable; explicit ruling/call; material data and attribution caveats.

BOUNDARIES
